**Invoke relevant or requested skills BEFORE any response or action.** Even a 1% chance a skill might apply means that you should invoke the skill to check. If an invoked skill turns out to be wrong for the situation, you don't need to use it.

Found the picture. Tracked files include items that shouldn't ship to a public repo:
- `.claude/settings.json`, `.claude/settings.local.json` — your local Claude permissions
- `.entire/.gitignore`, `.entire/settings.json` — session telemetry tool (CLAUDE.md explicitly: "do not author state there")
- `bash.exe.stackdump`, `codewalk/bash.exe.stackdump` — Windows crash dumps
- No root `.gitignore` exists, which is why they crept in

Your MEMORY.md memory `feedback_explicit_git_add.md` flagged exactly this pattern: *"persistent noise files will get swept in (README.md, .claude/, \*.stackdump, codewalk/.vscode/)"*. Cleaning these up before going public is the move you'd want.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- **`git rm --cached <path>` removes from the index without deleting the working file** — exactly what we want for files that should stay locally but stop being tracked. A plain `git rm` would also delete the file on disk, killing your local Claude config.
- **Root `.gitignore` is the "stop the bleeding" half**; without `--cached` removal, ignored entries that are *already tracked* keep being tracked. Both halves are needed.
- **VS Code extension repos commonly keep `codewalk/.vscode/launch.json`** because the F5 Extension Development Host launch config is part of the dev setup for collaborators. Your memory flags `.vscode/` as "swept in by mistake" — but for an extension repo, that file is genuinely useful, so I'm leaving it. Easy to drop later if you disagree.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

I'll write a root `.gitignore`, untrack the noise, commit, then create the public repo.

# CodeWalk

AI-guided walkthroughs of unfamiliar codebases, block by block. VS Code extension for COS 497 (AI Agents, Spring 2026).

This document is the **developer workflow guide** — how to set up, run, test, and iterate on the extension. The end-user README lives at [`codewalk/README.md`](./codewalk/README.md) and ships inside the packaged `.vsix`.

For project state and planning see [`docs/PROJECT_STATE.md`](./docs/PROJECT_STATE.md). For architectural decisions that deviate from the original design doc, see [`docs/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md`](./docs/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md).

---

## One-time setup

You need **Node.js 20 or newer** (for built-in `fetch` and ES2022 features).

```bash
cd codewalk
npm install
```

That pulls ~355 dev dependencies (esbuild, typescript, mocha, @vscode/test-cli). It takes ~30–60 seconds on a decent connection.

The first time you run the test suite, `@vscode/test-cli` also downloads a fresh copy of VS Code (~100 MB) into `codewalk/.vscode-test/` — that's a one-time cost, already gitignored.

---

## Daily development loop

### Step 1 — Open the right folder in VS Code

**Open the `codewalk/` subfolder, NOT the repo root.** VS Code's extension development tooling (F5, launch.json, task runner, etc.) looks for `package.json` in the workspace root — if you open `CodeWalk/`, it won't find one; if you open `CodeWalk/codewalk/`, everything works.

# CodeWalk

AI-guided walkthroughs of unfamiliar codebases, block by block. VS Code extension for COS 497 (AI Agents, Spring 2026).

This document is the **developer workflow guide** — how to set up, run, test, and iterate on the extension. The end-user README lives at [`codewalk/README.md`](./codewalk/README.md) and ships inside the packaged `.vsix`.

For project state and planning see [`docs/PROJECT_STATE.md`](./docs/PROJECT_STATE.md). For architectural decisions that deviate from the original design doc, see [`docs/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md`](./docs/ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md).

---

## One-time setup

You need **Node.js 20 or newer** (for built-in `fetch` and ES2022 features).

```bash
cd codewalk
npm install
```

That pulls ~355 dev dependencies (esbuild, typescript, mocha, @vscode/test-cli). It takes ~30–60 seconds on a decent connection.

The first time you run the test suite, `@vscode/test-cli` also downloads a fresh copy of VS Code (~100 MB) into `codewalk/.vscode-test/` — that's a one-time cost, already gitignored.

---

## Daily development loop

### Step 1 — Open the right folder in VS Code

**Open the `codewalk/` subfolder, NOT the repo root.** VS Code's extension development tooling (F5, launch.json, task runner, etc.) looks for `package.json` in the workspace root — if you open `CodeWalk/`, it won't find one; if you open `CodeWalk/codewalk/`, everything works.

content.text:
The harness blocked that as a destructive remote operation. I need to surface this to you — the situation is more nuanced than a straight push.

## Status

**Live:** https://github.com/AlexSharon04/CodeWalk (public) — pushed branch `phase2c-narrative-and-nav` (your full Phase 1–4 work).

**Pre-push hook hijack.** Your `.entire` telemetry tool installs a `pre-push` hook (`.git/hooks/pre-push`) that auto-publishes session-checkpoint refs to whatever remote you push to. On the first push it published `entire/checkpoints/v1` to your shiny new public repo. Future `git push origin <anything>` will keep doing this — your private session telemetry will leak into the public repo on every push.

**What's on origin right now:**
- `phase2c-narrative-and-nav` ← your code, intended
- `entire/checkpoints/v1` ← telemetry, not intended
- `main` ← not yet pushed (didn't push it yet to avoid re-triggering the hook)

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- **Pre-push hooks run on `git push` and can mutate the push set** — the Entire hook calls `git push` itself with extra refspecs, which is why one user-initiated push produced two remote branches. This is a legitimate pattern for things like sidecar artifact uploads, but it bites hard when remotes have different trust levels (public vs private).
- **The fix isn't `--no-verify`** — that only skips the hook for one push, leaving the next push to re-leak. The durable fix is either gating the hook by remote URL (`if [ "$2" != "https://github.com/AlexSharon04/CodeWalk.git" ]; then ...`) or pointing Entire's telemetry at a separate private remote.
- **Once a commit is on a public GitHub branch, deletion isn't full erasure** — GitHub keeps unreachable objects for ~90 days and forks can retain them indefinitely. For session-checkpoint refs containing session metadata you've marked sensitive, the sooner the cleanup the better.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

## Pick one and I'll execute

options.description: Edit .git/hooks/pre-push to only run Entire's push when the remote is NOT the public CodeWalk origin. Keeps local telemetry working everywhere else; stops public leakage. Then I'll delete entire/checkpoints/v1 from origin and push main.

options.description: Don't push main, don't touch the hook. Repo is up with the leaked branch; you'll decide the hook policy and finish the sync yourself.

questions.question: How should I handle the Entire pre-push hook before finishing the public sync (pushing main, etc.)?

options.label: Gate hook by remote URL (Recommended)
options.description: Edit .git/hooks/pre-push to only run Entire's push when the remote is NOT the public CodeWalk origin. Keeps local telemetry working everywhere else; stops public leakage. Then I'll delete entire/checkpoints/v1 from origin and push main.

options.label: Disable pre-push hook entirely
options.description: Replace the hook body with a no-op. Local commit-msg/post-commit Entire logging still runs; only the cross-remote push step dies. Simpler but global — affects future private remotes too.

options.label: Leave hook, accept telemetry on origin
options.description: Do nothing to the hook. The entire/* branches stay public and grow over time. Push main normally. Fastest, but conflicts with your CLAUDE.md '.entire is telemetry, do not author state' rule.

options.label: Stop here, I'll handle the hook myself
options.description: Don't push main, don't touch the hook. Repo is up with the leaked branch; you'll decide the hook policy and finish the sync yourself.

answers.How should I handle the Entire pre-push: i want everything in main, entire, all the latest features. my professor is going to look over the main branch of the code, and needs entire there explicitly
